sources.title: Sparkline theory and practice
sources.finding: Compact time series can sit alongside the number or text they contextualize.
sources.limits: Illustrations do not establish a universal accuracy or usability gain.

sources.title: Semiology of Graphics (1967; English edition referenced)
sources.method: Systematic visual-variable framework with diagrams, networks and maps.
sources.finding: Choose a visual variable that preserves the data relationship; keep categorical identity distinct from ordered magnitude.
sources.limits: The publisher summary identifies the framework; it is not a controlled performance comparison.

sources.title: Graphical Perception (1984)
sources.method: Participants estimated relative magnitudes from different elementary graphical encodings; estimation error compared by encoding.
sources.finding: For exact magnitude comparisons, prefer position on a common scale over less directly comparable encodings such as angle or area.
sources.limits: Task-specific ranking; not a ranking of all chart types, audiences or analytical goals.

sources.title: Crowdsourcing Graphical Perception (2010)
sources.method: Crowdsourced replication of spatial and luminance tasks; additional experiments on rectangles, chart size and gridline spacing.
sources.finding: Prior spatial-encoding findings largely replicated; rendering geometry and chart dimensions are testable factors.
sources.limits: Crowd study and simplified stimuli do not substitute for accessibility or product-domain testing.

sources.title: A Nested Model for Visualization Design and Validation (2009)
sources.method: Separates domain characterization, data/task abstraction, encoding/interaction, and algorithm; maps validity threats to evaluation methods.
sources.finding: Match evaluation to the layer of the design claim. Fast rendering does not show that the right question is being answered.
sources.limits: Framework for selecting evaluation methods, not experimental proof of any encoding.

sources.title: ColorBrewer.org (2003)
sources.method: Palette selection system based on data class, class count and viewing environment.
sources.finding: Use sequential schemes for ordered magnitude, diverging schemes for a meaningful center and qualitative schemes for categories.
sources.limits: Originally designed for maps; verify palette behavior on the downstream surface.

sources.authors: Jeffrey Heer, Nicholas Kong and Maneesh Agrawala
sources.title: Sizing the Horizon (2009)
sources.method: Compared time-series value estimation across line, mirrored and layered displays at different heights.
sources.finding: At small tested heights some layered variants retained accuracy better; relative performance depended on height and design.
sources.limits: Does not establish a universal pixel threshold or show that horizon graphs outperform ordinary lines at every size.

sources.title: What Makes a Visualization Memorable? (2013)
sources.method: Rapid visual recognition experiment treating visualizations as images.
sources.finding: Recognition varies with visual characteristics; memorability is a separate outcome from analytical accuracy.
sources.limits: Image recognition does not establish comprehension, useful recall, or better decision-making.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2
sources.method: Accessibility success criteria, including non-text alternatives, use of color, keyboard access and hover/focus behavior.
sources.finding: Equivalent access must not depend on color or pointer hover alone.
sources.limits: Conformance requires testing the actual implementation against applicable criteria; a palette or library does not certify it.
